newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: GOLF-GILFORD BOOSTS HIS RYDER CUP HOPES.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-GILFORD BOOSTS HIS RYDER CUP HOPES.

text.p: England's David Gilford took over the lead in the rain-hit Dutch Open on Friday to boost his bid to get into Europe's Ryder Cup team at Valderrama in September.

As one of Europe's successful 12 in 1995 against the United States at Oak Hill, the quiet Englishman has made no secret of the fact that he wants another taste of Ryder Cup action and a second-round two-under-par 69 for eight-under-par 134 earned him the early lead at Hilversum by a stroke.

After playing his second round he was ahead of fellow Britons Robert Coles, the overnight leader who had not started his round by the time Gilford came in, and Russell Claydon and Spain's Miguel Angel Jimenez.

While Gilford, who is currently lying 19th in Europe's Ryder rankings and reckons that he needs 'one-and-a-bit wins' to seal his place, increased his Valderrama chances, his fellow Briton Sam Torrance produced the performance of the morning as he, too, battled for an automatic place in Severiano Ballesteros's team.

Torrance, who is 13th in the table and nearly did not play this event because of a shoulder strain, came back from an early double bogey in pouring rain which dragged him five over par, to almost certainly make the cut on level par 142 with a stunning finish for a 68.
The 43-year-old Scot picked up five birdies after his double, including two over the last three holes which got him into the weekend -- a chip-in on the 16th and a 10-foot putt on the last.

Defending champion Mark McNulty, though, retired after six painful holes, suffering an aggravated back injury and the Zimbabwean is now doubtful for Monday's international qualifying section of the lucrative Andersen Consulting world championship in the United States.
